paragraphs.source_en:
ii 5. the wonder of her kind] S. first wrote ‘a Spirit descended from Heaven’ (Nbk 11 137).
 ii 6. lovely mind] Cp. Claire Clairmont’s appreciation of Lady Mountcashell: ‘Her countenance beamed
mildly, with the expression of a refined, cultivated, and highly cheerful mind’ (Dowden Life ii 317).
 ii 6–7. The belief that mental and spiritual qualities influence appearance and bearing hardly needs
referring to a source; interesting parallels have nonetheless been noted in S.’s reading. Butter (1970)
cites Plato, Republic (Mary Jnl i 230): ‘the good soul, by her own excellence, improves the body as far
as this may be possible’; while Webb (1995) cites Mary Wollstonecraft, A Vindication of the Rights of
Woman (1792): ‘that superior gracefulness which is truly the expression of the mind’.
 ii 6. upborne] Both ‘sustained’ and ‘elevated’.
 ii 8. Cp. OL (Longman iii 378–418, no. 322) ‘like unfolded flowers beneath the sea’ (54) and OWW
